meta.task: R12 isolated redrive — battery name Simplex Realty (BSE 503229, SIMPLXREA)

step1_resolve_by_name.verdict: PASS — clean single-match resolve, correct exchange (BSE), correct yahoo_symbol suffix supplied for downstream use.

step2_resolve_by_bse_code.verdict: FAIL (unfixed gap, not one of the named D66-D68 fixes but directly relevant to the collection workflow) — resolving by BARE BSE scrip code alone ('503229') still returns a hard no-match with zero candidates. It only resolves when the company name is also present. This means an operator/agent who has *only* the BSE code (a very common real-world case — e.g. from a BSE announcement feed) gets no path into the system via /resolve unless they also know or supply the name.

step3_fundamentals_on_resolved_form.note: The task instructs calling fundamentals 'on the resolved form'. /resolve returned resolved.symbol = 'SIMPLXREA' and resolved.yahoo_symbol = 'SIMPLXREA.BO'. Both were tried directly against the REST endpoint (bypassing the agent) to test resolver-grounding at the API boundary.

GET /fundamentals/SBIN (control, NSE tic.note: Bare NSE tickers auto-resolve to .NS internally. Bare BSE-only tickers (SIMPLXREA) get NO equivalent auto-.BO fallback — this is an asymmetry, not a general 'always requires exact suffix' rule.

step3_fundamentals_on_resolved_form.verdict: FAIL on check (a) at the direct-API layer — /fundamentals/{symbol} does NOT resolver-ground. Calling it with the exact 'symbol' field that /resolve itself just returned ('SIMPLXREA') produces a bare unhelpful 404 with no 'resolved SIMPLXREA → SIMPLXREA.BO' note and no disambiguation candidates, exactly the failure mode D68 was supposed to close. It only works if the caller separately knows to supply resolved.yahoo_symbol ('SIMPLXREA.BO'). Worse, guessing '503229.BO' (BSE code + .BO, a plausible-looking symbol given the code-first user input in this task) returns 200 OK with contaminated/wrong data (mismatched P/E, mismatched 52-week range, garbled name field) rather than an error — a silent-wrong-data failure mode that is arguably worse than a 404.

additional_finding_growth_unit_scaling_b.severity: high — concrete numeric defect, ~100x understatement, ships to the user-facing brief and the final chat summary
additional_finding_growth_unit_scaling_b.verdict: CONFIRMED, likely relevant to D66 (growth cross-check) not functioning for this ticker
additional_finding_growth_unit_scaling_b.summary: The published brief and the final chat message both report 'Revenue growth (MRQ YoY): +32.9%' / '+33% YoY'. The raw fundamentals payload's revenue_growth field is 32.863 with growth_basis='mrq_yoy'. Cross-checked against two known-good tickers from the same sidecar/session (BHARTIARTL: revenue_growth=0.157 -> a sane 15.7% YoY for a mature telco; ICICIBANK: revenue_growth=0.669 -> 66.9%), the field is unambiguously a FRACTION requiring ×100 to become a percentage, not an already-scaled percentage. For SIMPLXREA that means the true figure is +3286.3%, not +32.9% — a two-order-of-magnitude scaling error.

corroboration.reference_pack_independent_calc: (8.86 Cr - 0.26 Cr) / 0.26 Cr = ~3307.7% YoY quarterly revenue growth (reference pack states 3207.7% — itself apparently a ~100pp typo/arithmetic slip on their own part, verified by recomputing (8.86-0.26)/0.26*100 = 3307.69 in python), from the tiny Q4FY25 base of ₹0.26 Cr revenue vs Q4FY26's ₹8.86 Cr.
corroboration.agreement: 3286.3% (sidecar) vs ~3307.7% (reference, corrected) — within ~0.6%, i.e. the two independent computations agree almost exactly on the true order of magnitude; the brief's reported +32.9% is off by ~100x from both.

additional_finding_growth_unit_scaling_b.why_this_matters_for_the_named_fixes: D66 is explicitly the 'growth cross-check' fix for tonight's rebuild. The fundamentals payload includes revenue_growth_computed / earnings_growth_computed / growth_computed_quarters fields intended as an independent cross-check against the raw provider ratio — all three were null in this run, meaning the cross-check had no second data point to catch the scaling/interpretation error against. Whether that's because the computed-growth pipeline didn't run for this ticker, or because the model never surfaced/used it, the net effect is the same: an extreme, base-effect-driven growth number was passed straight into the user-facing brief mislabeled by two orders of magnitude, with none of the caveating language the reference pack applies to the identical figure ('Base-period revenue is unusually small... so the resulting YoY% is extreme and not representative of a stable growth trend').
